validated_results.title: Polyphenols: key issues involved in chemoprevention of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of polyphenol chemoprevention mechanisms rather than an original human study of resveratrol and incident prostate cancer.

validated_results.title: Tea consumption and the risk of overall and grade specific prostate cancer: a large prospective cohort study of Scottish men.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of Scottish men reporting hazard ratios for tea consumption and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: ≥7 cups of tea per day versus baseline 0-3 cups/day
extraction.timing: prospective, follow-up up to 37 years (1970-1973 enrollment to December 31, 2007)
extraction.population: Men enrolled in the Collaborative Cohort Study

sample_size.excerpt: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 6,016 men who were enrolled in the Collaborative Cohort Study between 1970 and 1973 and followed up to December 31, 2007.

effect_size.excerpt: The association was greatest among men who drank ≥ 7 cups of tea per day (HR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.06 to 2.12), compared with the baseline of 0-3 cups/day. However, we did not find any significant association between tea intake and low- (Gleason <7) or high-grade (Gleason 8-10) prostate cancer incidence.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The association was greatest among men who drank ≥ 7 cups of tea per day (HR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.06 to 2.12), compared with the baseline of 0-3 cups/day.
